title: rcapsule Architecture
text: rcapsule bridges reproducibility gap R package lockfiles (renv.lock) underlying operating system, native libraries, compiled scientific toolchains, output verification required durable open science production deployment. Design principles: 1. Deterministic & Offline-First: Static scanning, system dependency resolution, container compilation, linting, cryptographic manifest generation, local sandbox verification execute deterministically zero external network calls required. 2. Composable S3 Pipeline: Every stage produces transparent, inspectable S3 object (rcapsule_scan, rcapsule_spec, rcapsule_lint, rcapsule_manifest, rcapsule_verification, rcapsule_certificate) can used independently orchestrated end--end via build_capsule(). 3. Security & Reproducibility Default: Generated containers pin explicit base image tags/digests (never :latest), clean apt caches, order dependency layers ahead source code Docker layer caching, drop root privileges (USER capsule), support -new-privileges multi-service stacks. 4. Verifiable Provenance: Every capsule manifest (capsule.json) canonicalized hashed (content_digest) optional keyed HMAC-SHA256 signing (openssl::sha256), enabling tamper detection across metadata, environment specs, seeds, inputs, scripts, container definitions, generated outputs. 5. Tolerance-Aware Scientific Auditing: Reproducibility checks fast-path exact SHA-256 matches fall back structured numeric-tolerance comparators tabular (csv/tsv), json, rds outputs (handling floating-point BLAS differences Monte Carlo tolerances transparently).

title: Security Policy & Red-Team Hardening Audits
text: rcapsule frequently inspects, compiles, verifies untrusted third-party research repositories (e.g., peer-review replication packages, student submissions, external scientific pipelines). Accordingly, rcapsule defends four primary attack surfaces: Container Specification Injection: Maliciously crafted DESCRIPTION, renv.lock, requirements.txt, filenames, version strings, user-supplied parameters injecting arbitrary Dockerfile RUN layers, shell commands ($(...), backticks, ;, &&, |), YAML keys/anchors, Apptainer %post sections. Path Traversal & Symlink Escape: Relative ../ paths, --root absolute paths, symbolic links pointing outside project directory (e.g., /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/id_rsa) scanned, hashed capsule.json, staged sandbox, executed entrypoints. Sandbox Secret Exfiltration & Output Spoofing: Executed R scripts reading ambient host credentials (AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, *_SECRET*, *_TOKEN*) inherited parent R session, tampering capsule.json, timing side channels MAC comparisons, dropping undeclared extra artifacts. Report XSS & YAML Deserialization: Untrusted project names, git branch names, file paths, diff diagnostics, htmltools::HTML() objects injecting executable <script> / event-handler payloads rendered HTML5 Markdown verification certificates, YAML !expr tags executing arbitrary R code parsing.

title: Troubleshooting Reproducibility: Tolerances, .Rprofile Traps, and Cross-Architecture Builds
text: Even well-intentioned R projects fail reproduce subtle real-world ways. guide covers four common failure modes—rcapsule detects resolves one: Hidden .Rprofile portability hazards (machine-specific .libPaths(), setwd(), hardcoded API keys). Apple Silicon (linux/arm64) vs. HPC/Cloud (linux/amd64) architecture mismatches slow source-package builds. Monte Carlo BLAS floating-point drift requiring explicit per-file numeric tolerances (atol/rtol). Non-deterministic binary/plot metadata (embedded timestamps PNG/PDF graphics) unexpected extra artifacts.

what: 1. Catching .Rprofile Portability Traps and targets / here Projects
title: Troubleshooting Reproducibility: Tolerances, .Rprofile Traps, and Cross-Architecture Builds
text: Local .Rprofile files often silently break containers copied another machine. scan_project() inspects .Rprofile (ignoring benign source("renv/activate.R") lines) surfaces concrete hazards alongside targets pipelines, ::() markers, zero-byte files, unusual filenames: _targets.R detected entrypoint, compile_dockerfile() compile_apptainer() automatically emit targets::tar_make() container command:
code: library(rcapsule)  proj <- tempfile("rcapsule_troubleshoot_") dir.create(file.path(proj, "data"), recursive = TRUE)  writeLines(   c(     "source('renv/activate.R')",     ".libPaths('/Users/alex/R/custom-lib')",     "setwd('/Users/alex/Desktop/my-paper')",     "Sys.setenv(GITHUB_TOKEN = 'ghp_do_not_commit_me')"   ),   file.path(proj, ".Rprofile") )  writeLines(   c(     "library(targets)",     "library(here)",     "list(tar_target(clean, read.csv(here::here('data', 'survey wave 1.csv'))))"   ),   file.path(proj, "_targets.R") ) writeLines("", file.path(proj, ".here")) write.csv(data.frame(id = 1:3, y = c(1, 2, 3)),           file.path(proj, "data", "survey wave 1.csv"), row.names = FALSE)  sc <- scan_project(proj) sc$rprofile_hazards #> # A tibble: 5 × 4 #>    line hazard               severity message                                    #>   <int> <chr>                <chr>    <chr>                                      #> 1     2 custom_libpaths      warning  .Rprofile modifies .libPaths(); hardcoded… #> 2     2 hardcoded_local_path warning  .Rprofile references a machine-specific a… #> 3     3 setwd_call           error    .Rprofile calls setwd(); use relative pat… #> 4     3 hardcoded_local_path warning  .Rprofile references a machine-specific a… #> 5     4 secret_in_rprofile   error    .Rprofile sets an apparent secret/token v… sc$has_targets #> [1] TRUE sc$uses_here #> [1] TRUE sc$unusual_filenames #> [1] "data/survey wave 1.csv" df_tar <- compile_dockerfile(sc, r_version = "4.4.1") tail(df_tar$lines, 5) #> [1] "COPY --chown=capsule:capsule . /capsule/"                                  #> [2] "USER capsule"                                                              #> [3] "HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \\" #> [4] "    CMD Rscript -e \"quit(status = 0)\" || exit 1"                         #> [5] "CMD [\"Rscript\", \"-e\", \"targets::tar_make()\"]"

what: 2. Apple Silicon (arm64) vs. HPC (amd64) & Posit PPM Binaries
title: Troubleshooting Reproducibility: Tolerances, .Rprofile Traps, and Cross-Architecture Builds
text: Developers Apple Silicon laptops (arm64) frequently deploy containers x86_64 cloud hosts university HPC clusters (amd64). scan_project() records host architecture hints scan$architecture, compile_dockerfile() compile_compose() support explicit platform pinning plus Posit Package Manager (use_ppm = TRUE) binary repositories: Passing use_ppm = FALSE switches back source package snapshots compiling custom system libraries niche architectures.

what: 3. Configuring Exact vs. Per-File Monte Carlo Tolerances
title: Troubleshooting Reproducibility: Tolerances, .Rprofile Traps, and Cross-Architecture Builds
text: Deterministic summary tables verify bit--bit (atol = 0, rtol = 0), MCMC posterior summaries cross-BLAS matrix decompositions may warrant explicit numeric tolerances. compare_artifacts() create_capsule_manifest() support nested JSON, RDS (including matrices, data frames, NA/NaN/Inf alignment), CSV, TSV tolerances via atol/rtol (abs_tol/rel_tol):
code: f_ref <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") f_run <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")  baseline <- list(   posterior_mean = c(alpha = 1.2500, beta = -0.4000),   cov_matrix = matrix(c(0.04, 0.01, 0.01, 0.09), nrow = 2),   diagnostics = list(rhat = c(1.001, 1.002), divergent = 0L) ) reproduced <- baseline reproduced$posterior_mean <- c(alpha = 1.2503, beta = -0.3998) reproduced$cov_matrix[1, 2] <- 0.0102  saveRDS(baseline, f_ref) saveRDS(reproduced, f_run)  # Strict zero tolerance fails on SHA-256 mismatch compare_artifacts(f_ref, f_run, atol = 0, rtol = 0)$status #> [1] "mismatch"  # Explicit Monte Carlo tolerance passes and reports exact max observed error res_mc <- compare_artifacts(f_ref, f_run, atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-3) res_mc[c("status", "passed", "max_abs_diff", "max_rel_diff", "details")] #> $status #> [1] "within_tolerance" #>  #> $passed #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $max_abs_diff #> [1] 3e-04 #>  #> $max_rel_diff #> [1] 0.01960784 #>  #> $details #> [1] "Verified within tolerance (max_abs_diff=3e-04, max_rel_diff=0.01961)."

what: 4. Handling Non-Deterministic Plot Metadata & Extra Artifacts
title: Troubleshooting Reproducibility: Tolerances, .Rprofile Traps, and Cross-Architecture Builds
text: Binary PDF PNG files often embed creation timestamps graphics-engine metadata change SHA-256 digests across OS versions even plotted data identical. Best practice rcapsule: Always save underlying numerical data table (results/fig1_data.csv .rds) alongside rendered figure register numerical table outputs exact tolerance bounds. Use strict_outputs = TRUE verify_capsule() CI gating catch scripts unexpectedly drop temporary files log artifacts workspace. Keep ambient host secrets safe: verify_capsule(..., scrub_secrets = TRUE) automatically strips AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, credential variables executing isolated sandbox.
